text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the tool outputs, and the 'inconclusive' leaning and cautious tone fit the evidence. The core facts are present: 19.7% vs 5.3% expected, 0 of 6 documented 99215s below billed, 7 of 26 data-review notes without a lab line. But the narrative has internal tension and unsupported claims. The cited examples are weak and the next steps are generic, so an investigator would need to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Unsupported claim: '99215 is about 2-3x peers at every complexity level' is not shown on the card. The by_complexity table gives the provider's share vs all-provider share, and the ratios there run from about 1.4x to 2.5x, so '2-3x' is overstated.","'The notes may be written up to match the bill' is speculative inference from 7 of 26 notes with no lab line on the claim. The claim is hedged but goes beyond the evidence, and the missing-lab line may simply reflect labs ordered elsewhere.","The rationale contradicts itself: it says the charts support billing and 'no chart was below billed', then raises suspicion about note authenticity. It repeats the 7 of 26 point twice and leaves the headline and the rationale pulling in different directions.","Only two cited examples, both low-complexity 99215 claims with weak specificity (e.g. a 1-condition hypothyroidism patient). Neither is tied to a documentation finding, and no documented-and-supported 99215 claim is used for contrast.","Next steps are generic: 'larger sample' and 're-screen'. The text itself names a targeted coder review of low-complexity 99215s, but that is not in next_steps, and no specific claim IDs are named for record requests.","The 'too thin to judge' line sits oddly beside 30 of 30 usable charts. Only 6 were 99215, so the thinness is real, but the summary does not explain that clearly.","The rate of 14% for comparison providers matches the 0.143 card figure, but it is described only vaguely."]}
